notes.title: Update BETA 0.62_V5.5.6 : Asynchronous IO Supported
notes.notes:
[b]Update Details[/b]:

[list]
[*] [b]Fixed lag and crashes when saving large maps[/b].
[*] Added support for [b]asynchronous game data saving[/b].
[*] Fixed a severe bug causing saved games to disappear and preventing new saves.
[*] Resolved issues with DirectX12 not launching.
[/list]

Regarding the save-related problems reported by players, I've investigated and summarized the issues. Most of the problems were caused by game crashes during the save process. Due to the large data size of the world map, concurrent I/O operations during continuous saves could lead to lag and crashes. Changing the save process to asynchronous I/O effectively eliminates the lag during saving. Now you can confidently press 'F5' to save your game on the large map.

The issue of saves disappearing or preventing game creation also stemmed from individual save file errors. Most of these problems are fixable, and I've made the necessary adjustments.
Yesterday, some players sent error save files to my email, which helped me pinpoint the problematic code. Thanks! It helped a lot.


Concerning problems with the game not starting, I've done some investigation. It seems to be related to incomplete support for graphics APIs. If you continue to experience issues after updating, please feel free to provide feedback to my email.


If you encounter save-related problems, sending the error report of your save files to my email would greatly assist in identifying and fixing issues. Thank you!

C:\Users\YourUsername\AppData\LocalLow\LevenLiu\ZedZone

notes.title: ZED ZONE - APOCALYPSE AHEAD the Early Access version is now available on Steam
notes.notes:
“ZED ZONE - APOCALYPSE AHEAD” is a zombie apocalypse theme of top-view angle open-world survival adventure game, the Early Access version is now available on Steam, the first week have 15% off.

Catastrophe has arrived, You unfortunately trapped in the Zed Zone, where there are zombies and mutated monsters everywhere, want to escape from here, you must work hard to collect raw materials, upgrade skills, build shelters, defeat the wave of corpses and mysterious mechs, and finally find a chance to survive.

notes.title: Zed Zone APACALYPSE AHEAD will release on 3.29.2023 with Early Access.
notes.notes:
[previewyoutube=lMJ1gsAFTko;full][/previewyoutube]

My indie game "Zed Zone - APOCALYPSE AHEAD" has finally been released with Early Access. 
The game will be released on Steam on March 29, 2023 at 9pm PDT, in Early Access.
Thank you for your support and patience.
Your understanding and encouragement is my greatest motivation :D
 
If you are interested in the game, Please add it to your wishlist :D
 
Game description: Zed Zone - APOCALYPSE AHEAD is an open world survival and building game. Players have to survive in the zombie apocalypse world, scavenge for supplies, build bases, upgrade technology, and manufacture necessary supplies and equipment.
Explore this world, face danger and accidental death, and experience the joy of roasting in peace after danger.
 
And finally:
 
From the release of the first video of "Zed Zone" in August 19, to the video's 100,000 views, to the first version of the package, to the two internal tests, and now the upcoming "Early Access". I don't know, 4 years have passed quietly. I'd like to thank all of you on Discord and Twitter for your encouragement (and persistent reminders...) It really helped me.
 
It's not easy to develop an open world survival game like "Zed Zone-APOCALYPSE AHEAD" by yourself. The core reason is that one's mind is limited and can easily fall into a recursive thinking loop. This can lead to a period of time where you can't find the right direction, and often get stuck on a feature that's not really important. The biggest fear is not too much work, too difficult features, but an empty mind, no ideas.
 
Later, I conducted a small-scale internal test and received a lot of feedback, which provided me with a lot of ideas, and since then, development has been smoother than before.
So I think, for me, player testing is not just a formality, it is really part of development.
This is also the main reason why we choose to release it in the form of "Early Access".
 
In the future, we will continue to seek and refer to players' ideas and suggestions, and welcome players who like to pick up garbage in the end, to join us in the Early Access, to make a game that people love to play. That is the happiest.
 
 
Thank you for your continued support.
Thanks for reading. Remember to click on the coin collection after reading it :D
Thank you all! :D
